overview.text: Belarus, officially the Republic of Belarus, is a landlocked country in Eastern Europe on the western part of the East European Plain. It borders Russia, Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania, and Latvia, and its capital is Minsk. Its mostly low, flat landscape includes lakes, rivers, forests, and wetlands; the central Belarusian Ridge divides drainage toward the Baltic and Black seas. Belarus matters in modern European history as a former constituent republic of the Soviet Union that declared independence on August 25, 1991, during the USSR’s dissolution. Alexander Lukashenko became president in 1994 and has ruled since; the U.S. Department of State describes his rule as authoritarian.

key_facts.text: Minsk is Belarus’s capital, and the country borders Russia, Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania, and Latvia.
Belarus’s highest point, Dzyarzhynskaya Hara, is 345 meters above sea level.
The Belarusian Ridge is a watershed: rivers from the country drain toward both the Baltic Sea and the Black Sea.
Belarus declared independence from the Soviet Union on August 25, 1991; it had declared sovereignty in July 1990.
The United States recognized Belarus’s independence on December 25, 1991.
